summary: Validated decision-gated record for HiberFileSizePercent under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power. The clean Win25H2Clean baseline confirmed the current default, the repo power notes carry an exact docs hit, the residual string triage found an exact current-build ntoskrnl.exe hit, and the tools-hardened lightweight ETW follow-up surfaced exact runtime lines but not an exact runtime read. A later KVM local-KD follow-up then resolved the live hibernation symbol family, confirmed the current-build `Control\Power` registry path through `PopOpenHiberPersistedKey` and `PopQueryHiberPersistedRegValue`, and showed `PopHiberFileSizePercent = 0` on the running guest. Dedicated and recovery-backed KVM Procmon replays then captured real `Control\Power` activity through `powercfg.exe` and the `System` process, but still surfaced zero direct `HiberFileSizePercent` hits. A later host-driven KVM reboot observation closed the reboot gap by confirming a real boot-time advance while `HiberFileSizePercent` stayed `0` and `powercfg /a` stayed hibernation-unsupported before and after reboot. A QGA-launched WPR boot registry trace then produced an exact normalized `Registry / QueryValue / HiberFileSizePercent` event, closing the remaining runtime-read attribution gap while keeping the record research-only and non-actionable.

setting.name: Hiber File Size Percent
setting.casual_explanation: Hiber File Size Percent is a low-level power-manager value under the main Power key that appears to relate to hibernation file sizing behavior.
setting.why_people_change_it: Researchers track this value when studying hibernation support, hiberfil sizing, and adjacent power-manager behavior.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The lane now has a clean baseline value, exact docs and static hits, a runtime ETW lane that surfaced exact value-name lines, a live KVM local-KD inspection that confirms the current-build `Control\Power` path plus a running `PopHiberFileSizePercent = 0` state, repeated KVM Procmon replays that capture real live `Control\Power` traffic, a reboot-backed KVM observation that proves the value persists across a real guest reboot, and a QGA-launched WPR boot trace with an exact normalized `QueryValue` event for the value. The remaining concern is not runtime attribution; it is that this is still a raw power-manager value without a supported end-user tweak story.
setting.professional_notes: Win25H2Clean phase-0 existence confirmed HiberFileSizePercent on the live baseline with preview value 0. The residual docs-first static triage then tied the value to exact repo documentation hits, led by Docs/power/power.md:149. The shared residual string batch found an exact hit in C:\Windows\System32\ntoskrnl.exe. The tools-hardened lightweight ETW follow-up reran the candidate on RegProbe-Baseline-ToolsHardened-20260330 with a multi-trigger profile that combined hibernate toggle attempts, `powercfg /a`, and a file-I/O burst. That lane surfaced exact HiberFileSizePercent lines but still did not capture an exact RegQueryValue hit, so the candidate remained decision-gated at Class B. A later debugger-assisted KVM local-KD follow-up then resolved a coherent live hibernation symbol family including `PopHiberFileSizePercent`, `PopSetHiberFileSize`, `PopAdjustHiberFile`, `PopOpenHiberPersistedKey`, and `PopQueryHiberPersistedRegValue`. The same live guest run showed `PopHiberFileSizePercent = 0`, `PopHiberFileType = 2`, and `PopHiberEnabled = 0x00200501`. A string-dump follow-up resolved `PopHibernatePersistedRegLocation` to `\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SYSTEM\CURRENTCONTROLSET\CONTROL\POWER`, while the matching disassembly showed `PopOpenHiberPersistedKey` loading that path, building a Unicode string, and opening or creating the target key. The companion `PopQueryHiberPersistedRegValue` path then opened the same persisted key, queried a value through `ZwQueryValueKey`, and on `STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND` fell back to `PopReadUlongPowerKey`. A later KVM Procmon runtime replay with a dedicated `hiber-file-size-burst` produced a `267382`-row capture, surfaced adjacent live `Control\Power` activity through `powercfg.exe` and `System`, and still returned `0` `HiberFileSizePercent` fragment hits. A recovery-backed rerun then explicitly started from a closed elevated guest shell, reopened that shell through the hardened host runner, produced a fresh `245402`-row capture, reproduced the same adjacent-only `Control\Power` activity through `powercfg.exe`, and still returned `0` direct `HiberFileSizePercent` fragment hits. A later host-driven KVM reboot observation then confirmed a real boot-time advance from `2026-04-07T10:01:16.5000000Z` to `2026-04-07T10:09:21.5000000Z` while `HiberFileSizePercent` remained `REG_DWORD 0` before and after reboot and `powercfg /a` remained hibernation-unsupported. The 2026-04-12 QGA WPR boot-registry follow-up then captured a real boot trace, filtered it to registry hit lines, and produced a normalized bundle with one exact event: `operation = QueryValue`, `hive = HKLM`, `key_path = SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power`, and `value_name = HiberFileSizePercent`. That closes the runtime-read attribution story for the observed baseline value while keeping the record research-only rather than an end-user recommendation.
